question: Does one phase-calibrated real primitive-C3 response follow spin 4 or its real-C3 spin-8 alias under an equal-area physical rotation?

observer.normalizer: probability per paired configuration; the same Pinson-Arguin tau=i baseline is subtracted from both embeddings

production.common_field: the same counter-derived 130-bit Bernoulli vector is applied to both deterministic primal-edge orders for every replica

score.covariance: full paired 4x4 covariance of the mean from 100 batches
score.fit: GLS profile over one complex base amplitude and one signed-real gain per candidate

boundaries: An arbitrary complex gain for each embedding makes H4 and H8 unidentifiable; this production tests the explicitly frozen signed-real transport contract.
Common random bits provide paired covariance but are not claimed to be a physical edge isomorphism between the two quotients.
A selected phase law identifies this finite primitive-C3 transport rule, not a continuum field or the original square-site U by itself.
